low.setup: A kid has been following you for three corridors. He's waiting for you to stop. He's got something to sell, or to steal.

choices.label: Turn around and ask what he wants
choices.flavor: He sells you a tip about a nearby cache. It's real information. He was in the network before.

choices.label: Ignore him and keep walking
choices.flavor: He stops. He's waiting for someone else.

choices.label: Confront him directly
choices.flavor: He runs off. His hands had been in your jacket for two corridors.

low.setup: A traveling merchant sells things of dubious quality from a cart. 'Guaranteed authentic, certified original.'

choices.label: Buy something
choices.flavor: It's counterfeit. Functional. You'd have paid three times as much elsewhere.

choices.label: Haggle aggressively
choices.flavor: He enjoys the game. You end up with something decent for very little.

choices.label: Call out his counterfeits
choices.flavor: He vanishes in three seconds. The cart stays. You can take what you want.

low.setup: Someone drew a simplified map of the zone on a wall — danger zones, resource zones, obscure symbols.

choices.label: Memorize the map
choices.flavor: The marked resource zones turn out to be accurate. Someone who really knows this place made this.

choices.label: Copy the map onto paper
choices.flavor: You've got it. The information will spread less if it stays in your pocket.

low.setup: Two people make a quick exchange at a crossroads. One leaves with something. The other leaves with money.

choices.label: Approach the one with the something
choices.flavor: She refuses to talk. But she assesses your danger level. She decides you're acceptable. She offers you something else.

choices.label: Approach the one with the money
choices.flavor: He was looking for something else. You might have what he needs. Quick transaction.

choices.label: Do nothing — observe
choices.flavor: There will be other exchanges. This zone is active.

low.setup: An informal bar — a few crates, a barrel as a counter, and a woman selling something hot that resembles coffee.

choices.label: Order and sit down
choices.flavor: The hot stuff doesn't taste like anything known. Still comforting. She's chatty. You learn things.

choices.label: Order and listen to the other patrons
choices.flavor: They talk. People in bars always talk too much if you know when to shut up.

low.setup: An old scavenger repairs something ancient with modern parts. A strange hybrid that works anyway.

choices.label: Ask him what it is
choices.flavor: A pre-war navigation system. He's been restoring it for ten years. He explains what it used to map.

choices.label: Offer to buy the object
choices.flavor: He refuses. But he has other things to sell. Stuff he's picked up along the way.

low.setup: A crowd gathers around an argument — not violent yet, but close.

choices.label: Step in to calm things down
choices.flavor: Both parties accept the unexpected arbitration. One of them thanks you more concretely than the other.

choices.label: Take advantage of the distraction
choices.flavor: Everyone's watching the argument. Not you.

choices.label: Watch the argument through to its natural end
choices.flavor: It resolves itself. Crowds like this disperse fast.

low.setup: A guy offers you information in exchange for an unspecified favor — payable later.

choices.label: Accept without knowing what it is
choices.flavor: The information is good. The favor will come due at an inconvenient time. That's the deal.

choices.label: Refuse — vague debts are traps
choices.flavor: He shrugs. 'Maybe you're right.'

low.setup: A refugee from the latest purge hands you a photo of a station you don't recognize. 'It still existed three months ago.' He's not looking for pity. He's looking for someone who remembers it.

choices.label: Listen to his story
choices.flavor: He talks for a long time. What he describes matches nothing in the official databases. He gives you something in exchange for your attention.

choices.label: Give him credits without listening
choices.flavor: He takes the money. He watches you leave with something between relief and disappointment.

choices.label: Move on — you don't have time for other people's stories
choices.flavor: He keeps the photo in his hand. He's waiting for someone else.

low.setup: An independent technician has set up his workshop in a corner of the corridor. 'Quick tune-up, fair price, decent quality.' He seems to know what he's doing. Roughly.

choices.label: Let him work (full tune-up)
choices.flavor: Twenty minutes later, everything runs better than before. In places you'd forgotten about.

choices.label: Haggle the price down
choices.flavor: He agrees to half. The work is half-done. He's honest about that.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.flavor: He shrugs. 'Come back when it breaks.'

low.setup: A commercial delivery drone glitches in front of you. Its compartment opens and the cargo starts sliding toward the floor.

choices.label: Pick up what's falling
choices.flavor: Components, rations, an unidentified item. The drone flies off as if nothing happened.

choices.label: Report the incident to the station operator
choices.flavor: He thanks you officially. This gesture circulates in circles that value reliable people.

choices.label: Photograph the scene and move on
choices.flavor: Proof the company's drones are faulty. Someone will pay for that.

low.setup: A kid about ten years old plays alone with magnetic cards, reciting probabilities out loud. He knows exactly what he's doing.

choices.label: Play a round with him
choices.flavor: He teaches you a calculation system you hadn't seen. You lose. Worth it.

choices.label: Ask him where he learned that
choices.flavor: His father was a trajectory mathematician. He then points you to a shortcut commercial shuttles use.

choices.label: Keep walking
choices.flavor: He doesn't look up. He was already counting on you passing by.

mid.setup: A stranger sits across from you in a bar and puts something on the table. A file. He watches you.

choices.label: Open the file
choices.flavor: Your file. He knows things about you. He wants something in exchange for discretion.

choices.label: Push the file back without opening it
choices.flavor: He's surprised. 'You're not scared.' 'I know what's in that file.' He leaves. You might have bluffed.

choices.label: Attack before he speaks
choices.flavor: Violent. Effective. And now you have his file on you.

mid.setup: A local gang tests newcomers — not aggressively, just an imposing presence in your path.

choices.label: Pay the unspoken toll
choices.flavor: You give them something. They step aside. Next time it'll be cheaper because they'll recognize you.

choices.label: Walk past while ostentatiously ignoring them
choices.flavor: They appreciate the boldness, or the ignorance. Either way they step aside.

choices.label: Look them in the eye and wait
choices.flavor: A long silence. Someone in the group laughs. The tension dissolves.

choices.label: Draw your weapon
choices.flavor: That was a terrible idea, or a very good one. Both are possible here.

mid.setup: A coded message on a mural — an address, a time, a date. Three hours from now.

choices.label: Show up at the stated time
choices.flavor: An organized exchange. They were looking for someone reliable. You arrive, you look the part.

choices.label: Go there now to scout ahead
choices.flavor: You've got two hours' lead. What you find there tells you whether you really want to be there at the stated time.

choices.label: Ignore it — coded meetups in back alleys rarely lead anywhere simple
choices.flavor: Wise. Probably wise.

mid.setup: An informant someone recommended to you. He looks at you like someone sold him the wrong merchandise.

choices.label: Talk to him normally and see what happens
choices.flavor: He relaxes. He was expecting someone more dangerous. You get good information at a fair price.

choices.label: Play the part of someone more dangerous
choices.flavor: He buys the act. He lowers his price out of fear. Effective, and a little shameful.

mid.setup: A local faction is recruiting — a table set up, a sign, people approaching and leaving.

choices.label: Approach and listen to the pitch
choices.flavor: A well-trained recruiter. The pitch is good. The reality of what they're asking is less glamorous.

choices.label: Approach and refuse openly
choices.flavor: He tries to understand why. The conversation turns into a negotiation. You come out of it with something.

choices.label: Walk past without looking
choices.flavor: Recruiters note who pays attention and who doesn't. You didn't catch their interest.

mid.setup: A duel is about to happen between two people. Everyone backs away. Someone has to arbitrate.

choices.label: Impose yourself as arbiter
choices.flavor: Your intervention postpones the duel. Both parties now have to convince you their cause is just. That's information.

choices.label: Stay to watch
choices.flavor: The duel happens. The winner is generous in victory. He shares something with the witnesses.

choices.label: Leave before it starts
choices.flavor: Duels sometimes involve nearby innocents. Leaving is a reasonable precaution.

mid.setup: A reformed ship's doctor sells augmentations in a discreet corridor. 'Nothing illegal, technically.' His hands are clean. His smile, less so.

choices.label: Buy a stabilization module
choices.flavor: The installation is quick, roughly clean. It holds. For now.

choices.label: Buy medicine from him instead
choices.flavor: Less risky. Reliability unknown. Fair price for zones where pharmacies don't ask questions.

choices.label: Pass — back-alley doctors are traps
choices.flavor: Maybe. Probably wise in this particular spot.

mid.setup: A man in a hurry asks you to watch a package for an hour. 'I'll be back. Don't touch anything. Here's a hundred credits.' He's gone before you can answer.

choices.label: Watch the package honestly
choices.flavor: He comes back exactly on time. He gives you double. 'You didn't open it.' It wasn't a question.

choices.label: Discreetly open the package
choices.flavor: Classified data. Three people are looking for a copy. You now have one. Word will get out.

choices.label: Leave — not your problem
choices.flavor: The package stays there. Someone else will find it. Or not.

mid.setup: An informant being paid by two factions at once offers you his services. He's visibly very busy and slightly panicked.

choices.label: Hire him normally
choices.flavor: He gives you what he's got. Good information, partly true, carefully filtered.

choices.label: Use him to sell false information to his clients
choices.flavor: He plays along enthusiastically. Both factions now have false data. You have money.

choices.label: Report him to one of the two factions
choices.flavor: They appreciate it. His career as an informant ends. You're on their good list now.

mid.setup: A known fence in the area sells at rock-bottom prices — too low. He's liquidating everything. Someone's coming for him soon, and he knows you've figured it out.

choices.label: Buy quickly before it shuts down
choices.flavor: Fair price for hot goods. The quality's there. The provenance is murky.

choices.label: Warn him you saw the people coming
choices.flavor: He looks at you differently. He disappears. He left you something as thanks.

choices.label: Move along
choices.flavor: You don't get involved. What happened next, you'll never know.

mid.setup: A plainclothes military officer has been watching you for a while. He's bad at it. His posture gives him away.

choices.label: Approach him directly — 'You've been following me for three corridors.'
choices.flavor: He drops the act. He wants to talk to you about someone you might both know.

choices.label: Deliberately lose him
choices.flavor: He loses your trail. He'll note that you were hard to follow. Not a problem in every context.

choices.label: Carry on normally and let him follow
choices.flavor: He notes your routines. What he does with that depends on who he really is.

mid.setup: A lender approaches you with an unsolicited offer. 'I saw your situation. I can help.' He seems honest. Honest lenders are rare.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.flavor: He respects the refusal. He gives you his frequency 'just in case'. The pressure will come later.

choices.label: Take the money — debt now beats misery today
choices.flavor: The money comes fast. The terms come with it. Not exactly what he'd said.

choices.label: Ask him why he's approaching you specifically
choices.flavor: He has his sources. What he knows about you, and why he thinks you'll pay back — both are instructive.

mid.setup: A diplomat on a civilian mission is visibly out of his depth. His mission went badly. He's looking for someone to talk to.

choices.label: Listen — distressed diplomats are gold mines of information
choices.flavor: He talks too long. What he lets slip goes far beyond what he meant to share. Useful.

choices.label: Offer him practical help
choices.flavor: He needed someone who knows the station. What you make easier for him creates a favorable obligation.

choices.label: Pass — diplomats in trouble create diplomatic problems
choices.flavor: Wise.

mid.setup: A rumor is going around about a recently discovered treasure in the station — several versions circulate, all different.

choices.label: Cross-reference the versions to find the truth
choices.flavor: Half the people repeat what they heard. One detail comes up in every version.

choices.label: Search directly without wasting time listening
choices.flavor: You find something. Not what the rumor described. Still worth something.

choices.label: Ignore it — station treasures are always already taken
choices.flavor: Probably true. Probably.

high.setup: Someone who knows your name greets you like old friends. You don't recognize him.

choices.label: Play along — act like you remember
choices.flavor: He talks about 'what you did together'. You have no memory of it but the details are convincing. He gives you something.

choices.label: Admit you don't recognize him
choices.flavor: He's surprised. He shuts down. He leaves. You may never know.

choices.label: Question him about what he knows about you
choices.flavor: He assesses. If you don't recognize him, you're not the one he's looking for. Or you're a better actor than him.

high.setup: A death happened here recently — not an accident, people are talking, but the details change depending on who's telling it.

choices.label: Investigate the death
choices.flavor: You piece together the story. What you find is useful to someone who'll pay to keep it quiet.

choices.label: Ignore it — other people's deaths are rarely simple matters
choices.flavor: Wise. Extremely wise in this particular place.

choices.label: Talk to witnesses to understand the threat
choices.flavor: What happened here could happen to you. The details let you avoid it.

high.setup: A man is paid to guard a door. He's bored. He's also badly overpaid for what he's doing.

choices.label: Talk to him to learn what's behind it
choices.flavor: He talks. Bored people talk. What he describes is worth more than what he's supposed to protect.

choices.label: Pay him to look away for two minutes
choices.flavor: He weighs the risk. He takes the money. Exactly two minutes.

choices.label: Look for an alternate entrance
choices.flavor: There's always one in places that need it. You find it.

high.setup: A message on a private frequency from an anonymous source: 'Don't stay there. In ten minutes it's going to heat up.'

choices.label: Leave immediately
choices.flavor: Sure enough. Ten minutes later something happens where you were standing. You find out later.

choices.label: Stay to see what happens
choices.flavor: An operation. Armed people. You're in the wrong spot.

choices.label: Try to find out who warned you
choices.flavor: Someone's been watching you long enough to want you alive. That's interesting.

high.setup: A section of the station is clearly under a faction's control — markings, familiar faces, territorial body language.

choices.label: Walk through normally, ignoring the markings
choices.flavor: They let you pass. Your confidence, or your obliviousness, protected you this time.

choices.label: Verbally negotiate access
choices.flavor: They appreciate being asked. You pass with an informal obligation attached.

choices.label: Go around the zone
choices.flavor: Longer. Safer. Sometimes that's the right call.

high.setup: A faction commander you recognize by reputation sits alone at a table. He's seen you. He hasn't called his men.

choices.label: Go talk to him directly
choices.flavor: He appreciates the boldness. The conversation is short, precise, and leaves you with something to think about.

choices.label: Ignore him and move on
choices.flavor: He notes your face. Not necessarily a bad sign — people who don't look for trouble interest him too.

choices.label: Watch him from a discreet spot
choices.flavor: He's waiting for someone. Someone doesn't show. He leaves with an expression that doesn't bode well for someone.

high.setup: An assassination is being set up — you read it in the details, the angles, the positions. The target doesn't know yet.

choices.label: Warn the target discreetly
choices.flavor: She's surprised. She leaves without looking at you. Later you receive something from an anonymous messenger.

choices.label: Warn the assassins that you've seen them
choices.flavor: They assess whether you're a problem. They decide you're not, yet. They leave. The target isn't there anymore either.

choices.label: Do nothing — not your problem
choices.flavor: You walk away. Later, someone is dead. Maybe not who you think.

choices.label: Foil the assassination directly
choices.flavor: The clash is brief. The assassins leave. The target lives. Her gratitude is real and measurable.

high.setup: A signal on an unknown frequency broadcasts from a specific spot in the station. Short, repetitive. Artificial but not official.

choices.label: Locate the source of the signal
choices.flavor: A homemade transmitter in a bulkhead. What it's sending, to whom, and why — three questions each worth something.

choices.label: Transmit a reply on the same frequency
choices.flavor: The signal stops. Ten minutes later, someone arrives where you're standing. They look surprised.

choices.label: Ignore it — stray station signals have no known author
choices.flavor: Wise. Unidentified signals and their authors can be as dangerous as the curiosity they generate.

high.setup: A secondary faction leader contacts you directly. 'I've got a job. Clean. Fast. A favor in return.' He doesn't explain the favor.

choices.label: Accept the job without asking questions
choices.flavor: He appreciates the discretion. The job is exactly what he said. The favor turns out useful later.

choices.label: Negotiate details before accepting
choices.flavor: He answers some questions. Not all. What he clarifies is reassuring. What he avoids, less so.

choices.label: Refuse — factions and their favors are traps
choices.flavor: He notes the refusal. He won't hold it against you this time. He keeps the information for later.

high.setup: A local power vacuum just occurred — someone key in the area disappeared this morning. Everyone's waiting to see what fills the void.

choices.label: Quickly position yourself as a neutral contact
choices.flavor: Several parties come looking for you in the hours that follow. Neutrality in a power vacuum is a rare commodity.

choices.label: Find out why the person disappeared
choices.flavor: The answer has value to several factions. What you do with it will define you in this sector.

choices.label: Leave the zone before it gets complicated
choices.flavor: Wise. Power vacuums attract people settling scores in passing.

high.setup: A wanted notice about you is posted in the zone — not official, no known faction. Just your name and a reward.

choices.label: Tear down the notice quickly
choices.flavor: Two people already saw you. The notice is gone. Both people are still around.

choices.label: Leave the notice and find out who posted it
choices.flavor: The source is a faction you don't know yet. What they want from you isn't what the notice says.

choices.label: Leave the zone immediately
choices.flavor: Cautious. The zone will get dangerous in the hours that follow.

high.setup: An encrypted message was sent on your frequency. The content is ambiguous. The context suggests it wasn't meant for you.

choices.label: Reply to the message
choices.flavor: Someone on the other end realizes the mistake. They assess whether you're a problem. They decide to explain what it's about.

choices.label: Analyze the message to understand the context
choices.flavor: What it contains is a fragment of a larger operation. On its own, it's worth something.

choices.label: Delete the message and ignore it
choices.flavor: You received nothing. No one can prove otherwise.

generic.setup: A corridor you hadn't taken before leads somewhere unexpected.

choices.label: Explore
choices.flavor: A hidden room, a shortcut, or a spot no one's claimed. Useful in its own way.

choices.label: Keep going
choices.flavor: Another day, maybe.

generic.setup: Someone drops something and walks on without noticing.

choices.label: Pick it up and return it
choices.flavor: He's grateful in a way that goes beyond the lost item.

choices.label: Pick it up and keep it
choices.flavor: Ownership transferred by accident.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.flavor: It's not yours to pick up what isn't yours.

generic.setup: A local offers to show you something interesting they discovered.

choices.label: Accept and follow him
choices.flavor: It really is interesting. A hidden bit of architecture, a forgotten access point, something of value.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.flavor: He shrugs. He'll show it to someone else.

generic.setup: You come across someone who clearly needs help but isn't asking for any.

choices.label: Offer help without being asked
choices.flavor: He's surprised. He accepts after hesitating. What he was carrying — literally — feels lighter with two.

choices.label: Keep going and let him manage
choices.flavor: He'll manage. Or not. Not your business today.

generic.setup: A rumor is going around this sector — something happened, something's going to happen, someone vanished or appeared.

choices.label: Look into the rumor
choices.flavor: Half is true. The other half is invented to protect the true half. You untangle the two.

choices.label: Ignore the rumors
choices.flavor: Most rumors change nothing for you.

generic.setup: A quiet spot in an otherwise noisy station — a few unexpected minutes of calm.

choices.label: Sit down and rest
choices.flavor: Spatial quiet is rare. You enjoy it. You feel better afterward.

choices.label: Find out why it's quiet here
choices.flavor: There's a reason. Not necessarily worrying. But it's there.

generic.setup: You find a note — a word, a few sentences, left by someone for someone else.

choices.label: Read the note
choices.flavor: Intimate, private, not meant for you. It tells you something about the place you're in.

choices.label: Put it back where you found it
choices.flavor: Someone was expecting this note. It's still there for them.

generic.setup: Something fixable — a broken thing you could do something about with what you have.

choices.label: Fix it
choices.flavor: It holds. Someone who would've used it tonight will be grateful without knowing it was you.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.flavor: Not your responsibility.

generic.setup: An obsolete service automaton still runs in a transit corridor. It dispenses reconstituted drinks no one orders anymore.

choices.label: Order something
choices.flavor: It produces something hot. 90% reconstituted. But hot. It sends you a thank-you signal that might just be residual code.

choices.label: Examine the automaton up close
choices.flavor: Its maintenance panel has been open for weeks. What's still inside is worth something.

choices.label: Walk past without stopping
choices.flavor: It logs your passage anyway. Gives it something to do.

generic.setup: A handwritten letter lies on the ground in a busy corridor. No one's bothered with it.

choices.label: Read it
choices.flavor: A request for help. An address. Someone waiting for anyone to read it.

choices.label: Pick it up and look for the recipient nearby
choices.flavor: He's in the next corridor. His reaction to learning you read the letter depends on its content.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.flavor: Someone else will find it. Maybe.

generic.setup: A musician sings in an alcove with a voice that doesn't match his looks at all. People walk past without stopping.

choices.label: Stop and listen
choices.flavor: He sings an Old Earth song whose original version you'd never heard. He lets you stay for a long while.

choices.label: Leave him some credits
choices.flavor: He looks up. He doesn't say thanks. He plays better afterward.

choices.label: Talk to him between songs
choices.flavor: He's more interesting than his situation suggests. He knows people and places. He talks about it freely.

generic.setup: A couple argues loudly in a corridor. Passersby avert their eyes. The tone rises.

choices.label: Step in calmly to defuse it
choices.flavor: They both turn on you together, which ends up making them laugh. The argument resumes more gently after you leave.

choices.label: Keep your distance and wait it out
choices.flavor: It resolves without you. Some arguments don't need an audience.

choices.label: Offer your unofficial mediation
choices.flavor: One of them accepts. The other, less so. You learn something useful about their situation trying to help.

generic.setup: An informal barter market — people trading objects without credits.

choices.label: Join in — offer something
choices.flavor: The exchange is honest. What you get in return is different but equivalent.

choices.label: Look for a good deal without giving much
choices.flavor: The barter community remembers who's fair. And who isn't.

generic.setup: A network of informal passages connecting several sections without going through the official corridors.

choices.label: Take them
choices.flavor: Faster. More discreet. And you cross paths with people who use these passages out of necessity — instructive.

choices.label: Stick to the official paths
choices.flavor: Safer. You know exactly where the cameras are.

generic.setup: A malfunctioning holographic ad projects fragments of a pre-war broadcast. Faces that match no current era.

choices.label: Watch the fragments to the end
choices.flavor: A lost cultural context. A song. A recurring face you can't identify. It stays with you.

choices.label: Report the technical fault
choices.flavor: A technician arrives. He thanks you absent-mindedly. He'd known for two weeks.

generic.setup: A smell you recognize from something specific in your past drifts through the corridor with no apparent source.

choices.label: Follow it
choices.flavor: It leads to a makeshift kitchen. Someone's cooking something real in a station where everything is reconstituted.

choices.label: Stop for a moment
choices.flavor: The memory it summons is vivid. It gives you something the rest of the day didn't have.

generic.setup: A public terminal displays a message left by someone for 'whoever passes by here every morning'. You do.

choices.label: Read the message
choices.flavor: A farewell. A debt repaid from a distance. It's not for you but it matters anyway.

choices.label: Delete the message after reading it
choices.flavor: It's been read. That's all it asked for.

generic.setup: A child hands you something without explanation and runs off. A small, closed, unmarked object.

choices.label: Open the object immediately
choices.flavor: An encrypted message, a small valuable, or both. Someone was testing you or trusting you.

choices.label: Chase after the child to return it
choices.flavor: He was already far away. He was watching to see if you would. He saw you run. He nods from the far end of the corridor.

choices.label: Set it aside and keep going
choices.flavor: You'll open it later. Maybe.

generic.setup: An old soldier turned civilian security guard asks for your help with something trivial. He has no one else to ask.

choices.label: Help without making a fuss
choices.flavor: He's grateful in a direct way. He shows you something in the station no one else would have shown you.

choices.label: Politely decline — you don't have time
choices.flavor: He doesn't hold it against you. He finds someone else later.
